verdict.rationale: Ubuntu Desktop is downloaded and installed directly on the user's own hardware, either replacing or dual-booting alongside Windows, including on older machines and Raspberry Pi. That means the core product runs entirely under the user's control rather than as a vendor-hosted service. First-party docs cover the installation path step by step, from creating a bootable USB stick to installing and upgrading. Missing for 10: no evidence of self-hosting the update and package infrastructure (such as a local archive mirror or offline/air-gapped operation), and no independent hands-on corroboration of the self-install experience.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Download Ubuntu Desktop and replace your current operating system. It's easy to install in place of Windows, or run Ubuntu alongside it.
